The computational resource used in this study was the CATIA V5 software for developing the 3D models of the aircraft, and the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software, version 2012, for the electromagnetic scattering simulations.
The RAM material used in the simulations was FC70, which has good attenuation in the range of 10 to 12 GHz.

The RCS simulations were performed using the Asymptotic Solver (A-Solver) package of the CST software, with a Gaussian excitation, vertical polarization, and Triangular Mesh, generating around 2,000,000 elements.
The peak frontal RCS of the uncoated fighter aircraft was 15.2 dBsm, the peak lateral RCS was 33.1 dBsm, and the peak rear RCS was 30.5 dBsm.
For Scenario 1, the average frontal RCS showed around 10 dB of attenuation, the average lateral RCS showed around 16.6 dB of attenuation, and the average rear RCS showed around 5.4 dB of attenuation.
For Scenario 2, the average frontal RCS showed around 7 dB of attenuation, the average lateral RCS showed around 15.3 dB of attenuation, and the average rear RCS showed around 11.3 dB of attenuation.
For Scenarios 3 and 4, the application of RAM proved to be inefficient for frontal RCS reduction.
The average frontal RCS of the uncoated fighter aircraft was 10.2 dBsm, the average lateral RCS was 26.3 dBsm, and the average rear RCS was 10.5 dBsm.
The maximum detection range of the uncoated fighter aircraft by a typical radar was 222.5 km for the frontal aspect, 562.2 km for the lateral aspect, and 226.4 km for the rear aspect.
After the application of RAM in Scenario 1, the maximum detection range fell to 116 km for the frontal aspect, 216.2 km for the lateral aspect, and 124.8 km for the rear aspect.
After the application of RAM in Scenario 2, the maximum detection range fell to 169.8 km for the frontal aspect, 233 km for the lateral aspect, and 144.8 km for the rear aspect.
After the application of RAM in Scenarios 3 and 4, the maximum detection range reduction was less effective compared to Scenarios 1 and 2.
The difference between the theoretical and the measured reflectivity curve of the RAM FC70 is due to inhomogeneity of the material and the variation in the thickness of the sample.
The average frontal RCS of the uncoated fighter aircraft was 10.47 m^2, the average lateral RCS was 426.58 m^2, and the average rear RCS was 11.22 m^2.
After the application of RAM in Scenario 1, the average frontal RCS was reduced to 0.77 m^2, the average lateral RCS was reduced to 9.33 m^2, and the average rear RCS was reduced to 1.04 m^2.
